en: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, they said: Hatim ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from al-Muhajir ibn Mismar, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, he said: I wrote to Jabir ibn Samurah via my servant Nafi': "Inform me of something you heard from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." He said: So he wrote back to me: "I heard him saying: I am your forerunner at the Basin."

Al-Walid ibn Shuja' ibn al-Walid al-Sakuni narrated to me, my father—may Allah have mercy on him—narrated to me, Ziyad ibn Khaythamah narrated to me, from Simak ibn Harb, from Jabir ibn Samurah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "Behold! Indeed, I am your forerunner at the Basin, and indeed the distance between its two edges is like the distance between Sanaa and Aylah, with its jugs appearing like the stars."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, all of them from al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with this meaning, and he added: "its vessels are the number of the stars."

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me, 'Affan ibn Muslim al-Saffar narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, he said: I heard 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrating, he said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Men from among those who accompanied me will surely come to me at the Basin, until when I see them and they are brought up to me, they will be snatched away from me. I will surely say: O Lord, my companions, my companions! But it will surely be said to me: Indeed, you do not know what innovations they introduced after you."

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Ruzzi narrated to me, they said: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, he said: Anas said: The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "In it are seen jugs of gold and silver like the number of the stars of heaven." And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me, al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from Qatadah: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said the like of it, and added: "or more than the number of the stars of heaven."

Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us; (H) and Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani narrated to us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, both from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) the like of it, except that both of them were in doubt and said: "or like what is between Medina and 'Amman." And in the hadith of Abu 'Awanah: "between the two borders of my Basin."

'Asim ibn al-Nadr al-Taymi and Huraym ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us—and the wording is 'Asim's—Mu'tamir narrated to us: I heard my father; Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "The distance between the two sides of my Basin is like that between Sanaa and Medina."

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Anas ibn Malik narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The extent of my Basin is like that between Aylah and Sanaa of Yemen, and indeed in it are jugs as numerous as the stars of heaven."

And 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated it to me, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad: he heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said the like of it.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sallam al-Jumahi narrated to us, al-Rabi'—meaning Ibn Muslim—narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I will surely drive away men from my Basin just as stray camels are driven away."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan, from Thawban, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the hadith of the Basin. I said to Yahya ibn Hammad: "Did you hear this hadith from Abu 'Awanah?" He said: "And I also heard it from Shu'bah." I said: "Look into it for me," so he looked into it for me and narrated it to me.

Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and their wordings are close—they said: Mu'adh—who is Ibn Hisham—narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah al-Ya'mari, from Thawban, that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, I will be at the edge of my Basin, driving away the people for the people of Yemen, striking with my staff until it flows abundantly for them." He was asked about its width, so he said: "From my standing place to 'Amman." And he was asked about its drink, so he said: "Whiter than milk and sweeter than honey; two spouts flow into it supplying it from Paradise, one of gold and the other of silver." And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me, al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from Qatadah, with the chain of transmission of Hisham, similar to his hadith, except that he said: "On the Day of Resurrection, I will be at the edge of the Basin."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar al-Makki narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Abi Shaybah's; Ishaq said: informed us, and the other two said: narrated to us—'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-'Ammi, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, he said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the vessels of the Basin?" He said: "By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, its vessels are more numerous than the number of stars and planets of heaven on a dark, cloudless night. They are vessels of Paradise: whoever drinks from them will never thirst to the end of his existence. Two spouts from Paradise pour into it; whoever drinks from it will never thirst. Its width is like its length, from 'Amman to Aylah; its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Nafi', from 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, ahead of you is a Basin whose extent is like that between Jarba and Adhruh. In it are jugs like the stars of heaven; whoever arrives at it and drinks from it will never thirst after it, ever."

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me, Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of the hadith of 'Ubaydullah.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, they said: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, and he added: 'Ubaydullah said: So I asked him, and he said: "Two villages in the Levant, between which is a journey of three nights." And in the hadith of Ibn Bishr: "three days."

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, they said: Yahya—who is al-Qattan—narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah: Nafi' informed me, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "Indeed, ahead of you is a Basin whose extent is like that between Jarba and Adhruh." And in the narration of Ibn al-Muthanna: "my Basin."

Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani and Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us, they said: Hammad—who is Ibn Zayd—narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, ahead of you is a Basin; what is between its two sides is like that between Jarba and Adhruh."

Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah narrated to me, Harami ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, that he heard Harithah ibn Wahb al-Khuza'i saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying... and he mentioned the Basin the like of it, and did not mention the statement of al-Mustawrid nor his response.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Bazi' narrated to me, Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, from Harithah, that he heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "His Basin is what is between Sanaa and Medina." Al-Mustawrid said to him: "Did you not hear him mention the vessels?" He said: "No." Al-Mustawrid said: "In it, the vessels are seen like planets."

And Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Ash'athi narrated it to us, 'Abthar informed us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, both from Husayn, from Abu Wa'il, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to the hadith of al-A'mash and Mughirah.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both from Jarir; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, all of them from Mughirah, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to the hadith of al-A'mash. And in the hadith of Shu'bah from Mughirah: "I heard Abu Wa'il."
And 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us, from Jarir, from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission, and he did not mention: "my companions, my companions."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I am your forerunner at the Basin, and people will certainly be contended with me over, and then I will be overcome regarding them. I will say: O Lord, my companions, my companions! But it will be said: Indeed, you do not know what innovations they introduced after you."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Wahb—meaning Ibn Jarir—narrated to us, my father narrated to us, he said: I heard Yahya ibn Ayyub narrating from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Marthad, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) prayed over the slain of Uhud, then ascended the pulpit like one bidding farewell to the living and the dead, and said: "Indeed, I am your forerunner at the Basin, and its width is like the distance between Aylah and al-Juhfah. Indeed, I do not fear that you will associate partners with Allah after me, but I fear for you the worldly life: that you will vie with one another for it, and fight one another, and perish as those before you perished." 'Uqbah said: That was the last time I saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) upon the pulpit.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) went out one day and prayed over the people of Uhud as he prayed over the deceased, then turned toward the pulpit and said: "Indeed, I am your forerunner, and I am a witness over you. By Allah, I am indeed looking at my Basin right now, and indeed I have been given the keys of the treasures of the earth—or the keys of the earth. And by Allah, I do not fear for you that you will associate partners with Allah after me, but I fear for you that you will compete with one another for it."

Abu Ma'n al-Raqashi, Abu Bakr ibn Nafi', and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me, they said: Abu 'Amir—who is 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr—narrated to us, Aflah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Rafi' narrated to us, he said: Umm Salamah used to narrate that she heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying upon the pulpit while her hair was being combed: "O people!" So she said to the woman combing her hair: "Leave my head." ...similar to the hadith of Bukayr from al-Qasim ibn 'Abbas.

Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Sadafi narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr—who is Ibn al-Harith—informed me that Bukayr narrated to him, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abbas al-Hashimi, from 'Abdullah ibn Rafi', the freed slave of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that she said: I used to hear people mention the Basin, but I had not heard that from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). One day, while a young maid was combing my hair, I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "O people!" So I said to the maid: "Step back from me." She said: "He only called the men and did not call the women." I said: "Indeed, I am among the people." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, I am your forerunner at the Basin, so let none of you come to me only to be driven away from me just as a stray camel is driven away, so that I say: Why is this? and it will be said: Indeed, you do not know what innovations they introduced after you. So I will say: Away with them!"

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Mulaykah, that he heard 'A'ishah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying while he was among his Companions: "Indeed, I will be at the Basin waiting for whoever among you comes to me. By Allah, men will surely be cut off from reaching me, and I will surely say: O Lord, they are from me and from my community! But He will say: Indeed, you do not know what they did after you; they never ceased turning back on their heels."

Dawud ibn 'Amr al-Dabbi narrated to us, Nafi' ibn 'Umar al-Jumahi narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, he said: 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "My Basin is a month's journey in size; its corners are equal; its water is whiter than silver; its fragrance is sweeter than musk; and its drinking cups are like the stars of heaven. Whoever drinks from it will never thirst after it, ever." He said: And Asma' bint Abi Bakr said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, I am at the Basin waiting to see who among you comes to me, and people will be seized before reaching me. I will say: O Lord, they are from me and from my community! But it will be said: Did you not realize what they did after you? By Allah, after you they never ceased turning back on their heels." He said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah used to say: "O Allah, we seek refuge with You from turning back on our heels, or being led astray from our religion."
